name: Metoprolol
route_note: tartrate tablets twice daily; succinate extended-release once daily; IV in acute MI and arrhythmias
tagline: Widely prescribed β1-selective blocker for hypertension, angina and heart failure
summary: Metoprolol is a β1-selective beta-blocker available as immediate-release tartrate and extended-release succinate salts. It treats hypertension, angina and arrhythmias, improves survival after myocardial infarction, and the succinate form reduces mortality in heart failure with reduced ejection fraction.
mechanism: Metoprolol preferentially blocks β1-adrenoceptors in the heart, reducing heart rate, contractility and conduction through the AV node, and lowers renin release.

In chronic heart failure, long-term beta-blockade counters the harmful effects of sustained sympathetic activation, leading to reverse remodelling. Selectivity for β1 is relative and is lost at higher doses.
uses: Acute myocardial infarction and secondary prevention
Heart failure with reduced ejection fraction (succinate ER)
Rate control in atrial fibrillation (off-label in some regions)

history.title: FDA approval
history.detail: Approved in the US as Lopressor.

history.title: Toprol-XL
history.detail: The extended-release succinate formulation is approved in the US.

history.title: MERIT-HF
history.detail: Metoprolol succinate reduces mortality by about 34% in heart failure.

history.title: COMMIT
history.detail: Early IV then oral metoprolol in acute MI reduces reinfarction and VF but increases cardiogenic shock.

history.title: POISE
history.detail: Perioperative extended-release metoprolol reduces MI but increases stroke and death.

safety.boxed_warning: Abrupt cessation can exacerbate angina and precipitate myocardial infarction or ventricular arrhythmias in ischaemic heart disease; taper over 1–2 weeks.

facts: CYP2D6 poor metabolisers have several-fold higher exposure.
Metoprolol is one of the most-prescribed drugs in the United States.

references.title: MERIT-HF Study Group. Effect of metoprolol CR/XL in chronic heart failure. Lancet 1999
